note: the canonical grouping case: two runs of the same failure differ only in their numbers
the same failure one write later must land in the same group
an HTTP status is the identity of the error, not a variable
so a different status is a different group
markers are matched case-insensitively and accept separators
input: exited with code=17 and signal: 9 on port 49134
expected: exited with code=17 and signal: 9 on port 49134

note: an identity number long enough to look like a hash still survives
session and turn identifiers are per-run noise
a trace id, a span id and a commit are all hashes
absolute paths differ per machine and per checkout
a quoted value is treated as data — the documented trade-off that groups 'kanban' and 'security-scan' together
decimals are one number, not two
whitespace is collapsed and the result trimmed
a message with nothing variable in it survives intact
an empty message stays empty rather than becoming a mask
